Samira

Samira — thanks for the report and for the traces. We're routing this as a SEV-2. Our SRE and runtime teams are on a bridge; I wanted to give you an initial, customer-ready note while we investigate and to confirm we understand impact.

What we have so far (initial):
- Time window: ~07:45–08:20 PST, error spike and tailing elevated latency.
- Impact surface: intermittent 503s for ACME production inference calls (personalization).
- Mitigation in progress: we have temporarily widened routing to a lower-cost, higher-availability fleet and enabled prefix/KV cache bypass for affected model variant to reduce tail latency.

Immediate asks for ACME SRE team:
- If you have any additional traces with full request IDs, please upload to the shared drive link.
- Confirm if you prefer us to fail open to a cached variant (lower freshness) while we stabilize.

We will follow with an exec-friendly one-pager once we have root cause. ETA for next update: 35–45 minutes.

—Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: ACME SEV-2 bridge notes and ask list

Team — bridge notes (internal):
- Initial telemetry: a small subset of nodes on region-us-west-2 showed elevated scheduler queuing and repeated model-container restarts synced to kernel log spikes. Hypothesis: transient kernel patch + high contiguous sequence-length requests triggering memory fragmentation on a subset of quantified hosts.
- Immediate mitigations applied:
  * routed ACME traffic to dedicated preemptible pool with lower memory pressure (laura actioned).
  * disabled aggressive batching for ACME route to reduce peak mem footprint (jonas actioned).
  * rolled forward a conservative kernel parameter on the suspect hosts to reduce OOM sensitivity (infra).
- Customer-facing exec summary: needs to include: impact, actions taken, ETA for stable recovery, longer-term mitigations, and compensation ask if SLA breach confirmed.

Open internal asks (owners):
- Logs/metrics: get full container restart counts + kernel oops logs for 07:30–09:00 PST. (aditya)
- Permanent fix: propose quantization profile and batch/seq-length limits for ACME workload; engineering to review. (jonas)
- Exec note draft: please review the attached PDF (monica) and add any technical caveats. (laura)

Will sync on a quick 10-min after-action at 09:30 to confirm the exec note before sending to ACME leadership.

-aditya
Engineering Manager, Incident Response
From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmeretail.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: ACME Retail - executive summary (interim) — 09:12 PST

Samira —

Below is an interim executive-facing summary for your leadership and ops team. We will follow with a final postmortem once root cause is confirmed and the retro is complete. Please let me know if you prefer this in a one-page PDF instead.

Executive summary (interim) — 09:12 PST
- Impact: Between ~07:45 and ~08:20 PST, a subset of ACME traffic experienced intermittent 503 responses and elevated latency on personalization endpoints. Approximate error rate peaked at 4.2% for affected routes.
- Scope: ACME production traffic routed through us-west-2; subset of requests with long sequence length and larger payloads were more likely to see degraded responses. No data exposure reported.
- Actions taken (customer-facing):
  1) Temporarily routed traffic to a higher-availability pool to reduce queuing and restore successful responses.
  2) Disabled aggressive batching for the ACME route, reducing per-request memory pressure.
  3) Bypassed KV cache for the most impacted model variant to avoid stale cache pathology while we stabilize.
- Status: Traffic baseline largely restored; residual error rate has dropped to ~0.3% as of 09:05 PST. We will continue monitoring for the next 2 hours.
- Next steps (what we're doing and when):
  * 09:30 PST — internal retrofit meeting to finalize root cause hypothesis and timeline for permanent mitigations.
  * 11:00 PST — provide a follow-up note with confirmed root cause or clear next milestones.
- Ask for ACME: please confirm whether you want us to (A) fail over to a cached, lower-freshness model for up to 4 hours, or (B) continue with the current configuration with autoscaling limits tightened. Option A reduces error exposure at cost of freshness.

We apologize for the disruption. We're treating this as a priority and will include specific telemetry in the postmortem.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmeretail.com>

We'll upload the additional traces to the shared Drive. Once we have your final note and the postmortem, we can schedule a 30-min readout with our CTO on Monday.

Samira
